synopsis: As of 1 October 2026, ISO 19014-5 edition 1 was under publication for October 2026, replacing ISO/TS 19014-5:2021; its final text was received on 5 February and stage 60.00 began on 22 August, but the catalogue still listed the Technical Specification as the published edition [f2329, f2328]. Part 5 provides normative tables of required Machine Performance Levels (MPLr) for common functions, derived from the Part 1 method with derivation logic and assumptions [f10523, f2327, f2333]. Manufacturers can use these tabulated values instead of a full MCSSA for every new model only when the relevant use cases and assumptions hold [f2332, f12040]. The booklet recommends building the four-month validation plan around Part 5 tables and identifies them as the only sourced route to reducing per-model analysis burden, but it did not review whether collision avoidance or automatic braking has a table entry and found no published MPLr for that function [f2640, f15188, f2334, f2335]. Final contents remained uncertain because the texts were unavailable for review, and publication status should be rechecked before design freeze [f2862, f6286].
